disclaimer.title: External connections — Read before continuing
disclaimer.body_1: Connections allow your assistants to interact with external services (Notion, Slack, GitHub, etc.).
disclaimer.body_2: When an assistant uses a connection, your data is sent to the service via third-party software (MCP server) running on your machine. Apollia does not control this software's code.
disclaimer.body_3: Each connection uses an MCP server maintained by a third-party publisher. Verify the source before installing. Prefer servers from the official catalogue.
disclaimer.body_4: Use of third-party APIs is subject to their terms of service. Apollia cannot guarantee compliance of your usage.
disclaimer.body_5: You can at any time: require approval for each action, view the history of all actions, disconnect a service instantly, delete your stored API keys.
disclaimer.checkbox: I have read and understood this information

dashboard_header.title: Your command center
dashboard_header.message: Welcome to your dashboard. This is your central hub for monitoring everything in Apollia OS.

dashboard_agents.title: Active agents overview
dashboard_agents.message: This section shows your running agents at a glance. You can see their status and key metrics here.

dashboard_activity.title: Recent activity feed
dashboard_activity.message: This feed shows recent events from all your agents — actions taken, approvals requested, and more.

agents_grid.title: Your agent fleet
agents_grid.message: Each card represents an agent. You can see its name, status, and quick actions. Let's explore one.

agents_start.title: Start your first agent
agents_start.message: This agent is paused. Click the glowing Start button to activate it and see the runtime in action.
agents_start.success: Agent started! Notice the Chat button that just appeared on its card — you can use it to talk directly to this agent.

chat_discover.title: Start a conversation

chat_picker.title: Choose your mode

chat_libre.success: Chat session created! You're ready to talk.

triggers_overview.title: Automate with triggers
triggers_overview.message: Triggers let your agents run on schedules or react to events — no manual intervention needed.

triggers_detail.title: Your trigger list
triggers_detail.message: Here you can see your triggers. Each one ties an agent to a schedule (cron, interval) or an event (file, webhook).

approvals.title: Human-in-the-loop approvals
approvals.message: This is where your agents ask for permission before acting. When an agent runs a sensitive action (file write, external API call...), an approval card appears with details. You approve or reject in one click. The queue is empty right now — that's a good sign!

notifications_overview.title: Stay informed
notifications_overview.message: Configure notification channels to receive alerts about important agent events via desktop or webhook.

notifications_test.title: Test your notifications

observability_tabs.title: Three views of your system

observability_timeline.title: Real-time timeline
observability_timeline.message: The timeline shows agent events as they happen. The actions from this tour (agent start, chat, trigger) are already visible here.

graduation.title: Tour complete!
graduation.message: You've explored every corner of Apollia OS. You're ready to operate your agents with confidence.

dashboard.message: This is your workspace. You'll build and run agents from here — each agent is a Python module with a manifest() and run() contract.

agents.title: Start csv-data-worker
agents.message: Click Start to activate this demo agent. Watch how the runtime boots the Python module and registers it.
agents.success: Agent active! The runtime has loaded the manifest and started the run() loop.
agents.already_active: This agent is already running — the runtime detected it automatically.

agent_detail.title: The agent manifest
agent_detail.message: Every agent exposes two async functions: manifest() returns metadata, run() is the main loop. That's the full contract.

memory.title: Query agent memory
memory.message: Agents write to memory at their own initiative. Search the 'onboarding-agent' namespace to see what csv-data-worker stored.
memory.success: Memory results loaded — you can see what the agent persisted during its run.

chat.title: Chat with your agent
chat.message: The form is pre-filled. Send this message to see how an agent processes a memory-related query.
chat.success: Message sent. The agent will use memory.search() internally to answer you.

integrations.title: MCP integrations
integrations.message: Connect external tools via MCP servers. Your agents call these tools through the native client — no Python dependencies required.

triggers.title: Trigger types
triggers.message: Cron, interval, file-watch, webhook. Each trigger fires the agent's run() function automatically when its condition is met.

pipelines.title: DAG pipelines
pipelines.message: Wire agents together in directed acyclic graphs. Fan-out, fan-in, conditional branches — all handled by the pipeline engine.

observability.title: Observability
observability.message: Every tool call, memory write, and LLM token is logged in the audit trail. Use it to debug, profile, and audit your agents.

graduation.title: You're ready to build
graduation.message: You know the architecture. Create your first agent with manifest() + run(), install it, and let the runtime handle the rest.
